title: Add admin-controlled role promotion (User -> Admin)

requirements.text: Add a backend admin-only capability to change another user’s effective authorization role from "user" to "admin" (and optionally back to "user"), so that a user account can be promoted to admin and immediately gain access to admin-only operations (e.g., invoice upload and clear data).

quotes: How to account role user to admin

acceptanceCriteria: There is a new admin-only backend method that promotes a specified user to admin (and a corresponding method to demote back to user, or one method that sets role explicitly).
The method rejects anonymous callers and rejects non-admin callers with a clear "Unauthorized" error.
After promotion, the promoted user can successfully call existing admin-only backend methods (e.g., uploadInvoices, clearAllData) without changing any frontend code.
Role changes persist across page refresh and subsequent calls.
If the target user does not exist / has never been seen, the method returns a clear error instead of silently succeeding (or explicitly documents/implements the desired behavior).

requirements.text: Add an Admin-only frontend UI flow to promote/demote users between "User" and "Admin" roles, so an admin can manage roles without needing developer intervention.

quotes: How to account role user to admin

acceptanceCriteria: An admin can access a "User Management" (or similarly named) section from within the authenticated app UI.
The UI lists user accounts/profiles that exist in the system and shows each user’s current effective role (Admin/User).
For each listed user, an admin can promote to Admin and (if implemented) demote to User, with a confirmation step for role changes.
After a successful role update, the UI shows the updated role without requiring a hard refresh (React Query cache is invalidated appropriately).
A non-admin user cannot see or access this role management UI (attempts show an English access denied experience).

requirements.text: Align profile setup and role display so that user-facing role selection does not mislead users: remove or disable any self-service role selection that does not actually grant admin permissions, and ensure the displayed role reflects the effective authorization role used for gating admin features.

quotes: How to account role user to admin

acceptanceCriteria: If the current profile setup UI allows choosing "Admin", it is replaced with an English explanation that roles are assigned by an administrator, or the role field is removed/disabled for non-admin users.
The header role label and admin-only navigation visibility are based on the effective role used by routing/gating (not a user-editable profile field).
After an admin changes a user’s role, that user’s next navigation/refresh correctly shows admin UI (e.g., Admin Dashboard link appears) when their effective role is admin.

requirements.text: Add backend and frontend safeguards and messaging to explain how a "User" becomes an "Admin" in this system, using English user-facing text.

quotes: How to account role user to admin

acceptanceCriteria: Login/Profile-related screens show English guidance explaining that only an admin can grant admin access (no ambiguous wording suggesting users can self-promote).
When a non-admin attempts an admin-only action, the user sees an English error or access denied message that indicates they need admin permission.
Backend error messages for role-management endpoints are clear and consistent (e.g., "Unauthorized: Only admins can change roles").

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor; place all new logic in backend/main.mo.
Create backend/migration.mo only if state/schema changes require an upgrade path, following the project’s conditional migration policy.

Do not edit any frontend files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, or any files in frontend/src/components/ui; compose them instead.
All user-facing text must be in English.
nonGoals: Implementing third-party authentication providers (only existing app auth mechanisms are in scope).
Adding external databases or off-chain storage.
Building real-time role sync via websockets/push notifications.
